rejected.title: Judging sources
card: Author
the writer is named and has expertise in the topic, such as a climate scientist writing about climate.
Date
the source is recent enough for the topic. Facts about technology or health can go out of date quickly.
Purpose
the source is not made only to sell or persuade. A company page praising its own product is trying to sell.
Support
other sources back up its claims. If no other source agrees, be careful. A reliable source passes all four checks, not just one.
rejected.remember: Check author, date, purpose and support. A source you can trust passes all four.

a.q: Zane finds a page saying a new drink makes students smarter. A named nutrition scientist who works for the drink company wrote it. Which check does the page fail most clearly?
opts: Purpose, because it is made to sell the drink
Date, because the drink is new
Author, because a scientist wrote it
Support, because the drink is popular
a.why: The page comes from the company that sells the drink, so its purpose is to sell. The writer is named and has expertise, so the author check is not the problem. Being popular is not the same as other sources backing up the claim.
a.clue: Ask why the company made the page.

b.q: Priya is writing about a recent rise in teen sleep problems. Which source should she trust most?
opts: A named sleep expert's page from last year, citing studies
An unsigned blog post from last year, citing no studies
A named sleep expert's page from 1995, citing no studies
A mattress seller's page from last year, citing studies
b.why: The named sleep expert's page from last year passes all four checks: a named expert, a recent date, a purpose of informing, and support from studies. The mattress seller's page cites studies, but its purpose is to sell, so it fails the purpose check.
b.clue: Check all four things, not only the one that looks good.

draft.title: Judging sources
card: Before you use a source in your planning, ask if it can be trusted. A reliable source passes four checks: author, date, purpose and support.
Author

the writer is named and has expertise in the topic, such as a scientist writing about climate. Date: the source is recent enough for the topic, as facts about technology or health can go out of date quickly.
Purpose
the source is not made only to sell or persuade. A company page praising its own product is trying to sell.
Support
other sources back up its claims. If no other source agrees, be careful.
draft.remember: Check the author, the date, the purpose and whether other sources agree.

a.q: Zane finds a page that says a new drink makes students smarter. It is written by the company that sells the drink. Which check does the page fail most clearly?
opts: Purpose, because it is made to sell the drink
Date, because the drink is new
Author, because a company wrote it
Support, because the drink is popular
a.why: The company wrote the page to sell its drink, so its purpose is not neutral. Being new does not make a page out of date, and being popular is not the same as other sources supporting the claim.
a.clue: Ask why the company made the page.

b.q: Priya is writing about a rise in teen sleep problems. Which source should she trust most?
opts: A named sleep expert, written last year, with cited studies
An unsigned blog, written last year, with no cited sources
A named sleep expert, written long ago, with no cited sources
A mattress seller's page, written last year, with cited studies
b.why: The first source has a named expert, a recent date, a purpose of informing, and support from other studies. The mattress page cites studies, but the seller's purpose is to sell, so it fails the purpose check.
b.clue: Check all four things, not only the one that looks good.
